claims.statement: The BFF runs in three modes: local dev (Metro, port 8081, HTTP, non-Secure cookies), dev container (mcm-bff-service-nonsecure, port 8082, HTTP, non-Secure — the standard final local E2E run), and prod container (mcm-bff-service-secure + TLS proxy, port 8443, HTTPS, Secure cookies — reserved for future CI/CD, not a routine local step).

The dev-container run is the deterministic baseline for flaky-vs-broken triage (~54s for the current suite); Metro has JIT/long-session variance that produces misleading red herrings and must not be used for this diagnosis.
global-setup.ts asserts the X-BFF-Source header to fail-fast on a Metro false-green when dev-container mode is expected.

app-ci's app-e2e job runs test:integration for SIX projects — agent (movie-assistant), the three MCP servers (movie-mcp, spreadsheet-mcp, web-api-mcp, added by feature 048/059), mc-service, and mcm-app — before the web/APK/emulator legs, with MCM_REQUIRE_LIVE_STACK=1 that escalates a SKIP to a FAILURE; before feature 041 no project's integration tier ran in CI.

The BFF integration test harness uses testEnvironment: node and maxWorkers: 1 (serial) because tests share Redis db 1 and the live BFF — parallel flushdb/teardown would corrupt another file's data mid-test.

BFF integration tests acquire real tokens via the test-only mcm-bff-test ROPC client; calling ensureRopcAudienceMapper() in beforeAll is required for any test that hits validateJwt or mc-service, or ROPC tokens are rejected as 'Invalid token audience'.
route-coverage-map.ts fails the build if any +api.ts route lacks a test or justified exclusion; login PKCE is the only map-level exclusion.
preflight.global.js probes BFF, Keycloak, Redis, and BFF Mongo and throws when MCM_REQUIRE_LIVE_STACK=1 and any dependency is unreachable; locally the flag is unset and the guard is a no-op.

agent-e2e.mjs runs each agent spec file in a fresh nx e2e invocation (isolated per file) and does NOT work inside the dev container because chromium cannot be installed there; agent-stack.mjs itself works fine inside the container.

agent-stack.mjs fetches the gateway's confidential client secret from Keycloak admin via kc_admin.admin_token(), whose cfg() reads the process env first and then frontend/mcm-app/.env.local (then .env.e2e.local) — so after gen-dev-env.mjs nothing must be exported by hand; 'service-account admin token failed (401)' means that file is absent or stale against the realm. Setting AGENT_GATEWAY_CLIENT_SECRET skips the lookup entirely.

agent-stack.mjs resolveCommand() is a pure tested function that rejects any unrecognised argv via scripts/lib/argv-contract.mjs (PR #497); before the fix, --help and any typo caused the script to build and deploy the full agent stack.

The Playwright image tag must match the @playwright/test version the lockfile resolves; a mismatch causes ZERO tests to run and the e2e result gate reports 'no Playwright summary found'. The tag lives in three places with unequal weight: app-ci.yml (authoritative, 2 occurrences), devcontainer.md (3 occurrences), e2e-testing.md (1 occurrence). Enforced by scripts/check-toolchain-consistency.mjs in ~0.4s before app-e2e starts.

Agent E2E flows must never assert on a specific TMDB-ranked title; assert by list position (slot index testID such as disambig-option-1), never by hardcoded name. However, assistant-disambiguate specs hardcode the same film on purpose (load-bearing for substring regression) and must not be made dynamic.

The ownership guard (e2e-collection-ownership.guard.test.mjs) only matches request.post('/bff-api/collections') and does NOT catch specs that create collections via non-POST routes such as backup restore, import, or seed. Such specs must clean up what they caused to exist by name in afterEach.

On PR #527, backup restore left collections named '... (backup timestamp)' and 'Mutated e2e-...' in the shared test account; agent-disambiguation then produced a disambiguation question instead of a movie card and failed three Maestro attempts (~35 min each) — a cross-tier data contamination failure.

dev-realm previously had accessTokenLifespan: 300; it now matches ci-realm at 5400s. The globalTeardown fails any local run with refresh_rate_limited > 0. In the dev container the guard does not fire — run e2e-contention-tally.sh manually on the host after a containerized run.

A datastore volume that survives between runs fails the NEXT run, not the current one. mcm-bff-cache-redis-data was missing from the CI reset step; a Redis version mismatch between consecutive runs produces 'Can't handle RDB format version N' at bring-up. Fixed by adding the volume to both reset steps; app-ci-stateful-reset.guard.test.mjs enforces it.

Web E2E teardown deletes only what the test declared with ownCollection(), matched exactly or on an '<owned> ' prefix; forgetting to declare leaks the collection (bounded, swept at the next run start) rather than deleting a live fixture. e2e-collection-ownership.guard.test.mjs fails the build if a spec POSTs /bff-api/collections without calling ownCollection. Since feature 054 US4 each worker mints its own Keycloak identity and mc-service scopes collections by owner_id = token.subject, so name-scoping is now belt-and-braces rather than the only barrier against cross-worker deletion.

CI agent-flow failures ship full per-service container logs plus docker inspect health JSON as the agent-e2e-container-logs artifact before teardown; the artifact is the required first diagnostic step because containers are gone after teardown.
Bounded E2E retry is at most one retry per test (web: Playwright retries:1; mobile: maestro-e2e.mjs re-runs a failed flow once, logging RETRY 1/1). Additional retries risk masking a real defect.

Agent tests are classified by E2E_TIER: @gate (155 tests, blocking) and @model-decision (22 tests, non-blocking, main + dispatch only). An unclassified agent test fails the gate enforced by scripts/__tests__/agent-test-classification.test.mjs.
--grep-invert is accepted by Playwright 1.60 but silently does nothing; the tier split must be applied via E2E_TIER -> grep/grepInvert in playwright.config.ts, not as a CLI flag.

node --test <file> --test-name-pattern silently runs everything; Node stops parsing its own flags at the script path so the pattern is passed to the script as argv and ignored. The safe form is flags-before-path.

A pipe discards the exit code — cmd | tail reports tail's status (almost always 0). Use cmd > /tmp/out.log 2>&1; echo EXIT=$? or set -o pipefail. grep exits 1 when it matches nothing, so a filtered check can invent a failure.

A container reporting running at 100% CPU on one core is wedged (spin), not slow — a blocked await sits near 0%. movie-assistant-gateway has been caught in a livelock and now carries a healthcheck so docker ps says unhealthy instead of Up; it is NOT auto-restarted.

After driving an agent control, assert on what the assistant said, not client-local state. The Add button's disabled state is set by setActioned(true) in the tap handler BEFORE the agent has replied — it cannot distinguish any two agent responses.

Reply assertions must be scoped to ONE new reply, not the whole transcript panel. Count replies before and after the action, wait for count+1, then read only the last one. Include the assistant's decline copy in the negatives.
The Expo web bundle is baked into the BFF image; any change under frontend/mcm-app/src/ is invisible to a containerized E2E run until pnpm nx run mcm-app:build plus a container recreate.

The lifecycle Playwright project (bff-prod-lifecycle + admin-registration, 3 tests) has dependencies: ['chromium'] and never runs while the main project has any failure — these report 'N did not run', not a skip, and went unnoticed for months.
app-ci now runs node scripts/e2e-failure-set.mjs gate after the web E2E; it fails on skipped > 0, did not run > 0, or a log with no summary at all. flaky is still NOT observable on a green run.

The maestro-debug artifact's screenshot is the diagnostic that settles a mobile-tier data-leak failure (e.g. PR #527) in seconds, because the failure surfaces in a different suite/tier/language than the one that caused it and every local signal points away from the true cause. An agent working inside the dev container currently cannot fetch that artifact (item #531, unresolved) — so when a mobile-tier agent flow fails on an apparently-unrelated diff, suspect shared account/collection state before layout and list the test account's collections first.

Under MCM_REQUIRE_BACKUP_TARGETS=1 the jest preflight additionally probes the two feature-073 backup destinations from their own compose file — Backup S3 (RustFS) at ${BACKUP_TEST_S3_ENDPOINT}/health/ready expecting HTTP 200, and Backup WebDAV at ${BACKUP_TEST_WEBDAV_ENDPOINT} expecting 401. The WebDAV container is distroless and cannot self-probe, so this unauthenticated 401 is the only assertion that it parsed its config, is listening, and has auth configured. The flag is separate from MCM_REQUIRE_LIVE_STACK so suites that never touch the destinations do not start requiring them.

CI escalates a missing backup destination on both tiers: the BFF integration step sets MCM_REQUIRE_BACKUP_TARGETS=1 alongside MCM_REQUIRE_LIVE_STACK=1, and the web E2E gate forwards E2E_REQUIRE_BACKUP_TARGETS=1 into the Playwright container, after a dedicated app-e2e-bring-up-backup-destinations step brings the destinations up from infrastructure-as-code/docker/backups/compose.yaml. backups.spec.ts skips when BACKUP_TEST_S3_SECRET_KEY is unset, so each flag converts that skip into a failure where the targets are supposed to be up. S3/WebDAV credentials are minted per run and exported via $GITHUB_ENV, while BACKUP_TICK_SECRET is read back from the generated .env.docker rather than minted again, because a second value would 404 against the BFF holding the first.

playwright.config.ts caps workers at 10 (half the cores) with fullyParallel: false, and global setup mints one Keycloak identity and session file (user-<parallelIndex>.json) per worker, with a worker-identities.json manifest so global teardown deletes exactly the throwaway users it created — worker 0 reuses the canonical E2E_TEST_USER and is never deleted. One session per worker gives each refresh bucket exactly one client, which is what removed the measured 32-of-66 rejected-refresh contention of the single shared session.

docker run forwards ONLY the variables named with -e, so a gate-driving env var present in the job's env block but omitted from the list silently skips tests behind a green required gate — E2E_AGENT_PRODUCTION (all agent specs) and KEYCLOAK_SERVICE_CLIENT_SECRET (admin-settings-access, admin-registration) were both live instances. scripts/__tests__/app-e2e-env.guard.test.mjs asserts the forwarding list, the workflow enumerates the deliberately-omitted remainder against every process.env read under tests/e2e/, and secrets use the bare -e NAME pass-through form rather than -e NAME=$NAME, which would expose the value in argv.

ci-realm.json and dev-realm.json set accessTokenLifespan: 5400 while prod-realm.json keeps 300. A running Keycloak keeps the OLD value until the realm is re-imported, so an un-reimported realm still expires access tokens five minutes in and a local run past ~5 minutes re-enters refresh contention — which surfaces as 401s and 'gotoHome: home screen did not render', reading like an application bug.

scripts/e2e-contention-tally.sh is tally-only by default (it never fails) and takes --gate to exit 1 on any contention — the form app-ci invokes. The web E2E globalTeardown fails a local run when refresh_rate_limited > 0, with a message naming the token lifespan and the realm file to check, and reports 'could not measure' rather than zero when the Docker CLI is unavailable.

scripts/__tests__/agent-test-classification.test.mjs pins the tier PARTITION rather than the counts — union complete, intersection empty, both sides non-empty, no test in both tiers, and no test.skip/.only used to achieve the split — and asserts that app-ci runs both E2E_TIER selections with continue-on-error: true only on the model step, so a missing or blocking model tier fails the guard.

agent-e2e.mjs's recorded justification for running each agent spec in isolation (the full parallel suite sharing ONE test user, exhausting the per-user rate limit and crossing the access-token lifetime) is stale on both premises — feature 054 US4 gave each worker its own identity and dev-realm now matches ci-realm at 5400 s — while per-file isolation remains how the agent specs are run.
